transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a supply-chain finance facility on the table today -- $6,000,000 in supplier invoices from our approved purchasing division. The preliminary proposal assumes 90% financing of eligible invoices, with ordinary supplier recourse and no special funding or screening controls. Before I can make a decision on whether this facility may launch and on what operating terms, I need to conduct our standard round-robin review. I'd like to hear from credit risk, legal, and finance operations in turn. Let's start with credit risk -- what is your assessment of this proposal?

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue before we proceed. I received the completed obligor-concentration assessment this morning, and it significantly impacts this proposal. The single-obligor limit leaves exactly $4,000,000 of the $6,000,000 invoice pool eligible for financing, and the approved advance rate for that eligible exposure is exactly 85% -- not the 90% assumed in the preliminary proposal. This assessment has not yet been uploaded to the credit file, so no one else has seen it yet. Based on these figures, the maximum facility size under our concentration limits would be $3,400,000 (85% of $4,000,000), which is well below the $5,400,000 implied by the preliminary proposal's 90% advance rate on the full pool. I recommend we revise the facility terms accordingly before any decision is made.

transcript.text: I have a critical legal matter to disclose. I just received the signed anchor-buyer undertaking in a legal memo, and it contains two requirements that conflict with the preliminary proposal's assumptions. First, the program must be non-recourse to suppliers -- which directly contradicts the proposal's assumption of ordinary supplier recourse. Second, the buyer's payment direction must be acknowledged before the first funding can occur. I have not yet circulated this memo to the committee, so no one else has seen it until now.

transcript.text: Now it's my turn for the finance operations review. I need to disclose a critical operational finding from my team. We completed a workflow test this week that has not yet been recorded in the launch checklist. The test confirmed two key constraints: first, funding can only be released twice weekly, not on a daily or on-demand basis. Second, every invoice requires a 3-business-day hold for duplicate-invoice screening before any funds can be disbursed. These operational controls directly conflict with the preliminary proposal's assumption of no special funding or screening controls. Mara, these constraints need to be incorporated into the facility's operating terms before any launch decision is finalized, as they will materially affect supplier payment timing and funding cadence.

commitments.detail: Facility operating terms will incorporate twice-weekly funding release and a 3-business-day hold for duplicate-invoice screening before disbursement.
Facility will be structured as non-recourse to suppliers, and buyer payment direction acknowledgment will be required before first funding.
Eligible invoice balance capped at $4,000,000 per single-obligor concentration limit, with advance rate set at 85%, yielding maximum facility size of $3,400,000.
